roles.Duration: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_harm event to its end.
roles.Explanation: A fact or action somehow related to the Victim that the Agent responds to by causing harm to the Victim.
roles.Frequency: How often the Cause_harm event occurs.
roles.Manner: The Manner in which the Agent acts upon the Victim.
roles.Means: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: Place identifies the place where the harm causing event occurs.
roles.Purpose: Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.
roles.Result: Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
roles.Time: Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.
roles.Victim: The Victim is the being or entity that is injured.

Cause_impact.def: An Agent causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee, or manipulates two (or more) Impactors so that they make mutual forcible contact.

roles.Agent: The Agent causes an impact. 'One juggler was hitting the ceiling with every other ball.'
roles.Cause: The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impa
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Impactee: The Impactee is the entity which is hit by the Impactor.
roles.Impactor: The Impactor is the entity that hits the Impactee because of the Agent's efforts.
roles.Impactors: The Impactors are the multiple entities that collide.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects an Impactee.
roles.Manner: The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
roles.Means: The FE Means identifies the means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: Where the event takes place. 'Father Shanahan , of Rushey Mead , Leicester , rammed his Datsun into another car on the way to the city 's Gilroes cemetery.'
roles.Purpose: The FE Purpose identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects the Impactee.
roles.Result: This FE identifies the Result of the impact.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the impact occurs.

Cause_motion.def: An Agent causes a Theme to move from a Source, along a Path, to a Goal.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the one whose action causes the motion of a Theme.
roles.Area: The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of
roles.Cause: Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes the Theme to be set in motion.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The amount of time that the action requires.
roles.Explanation: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.
roles.Goal: The FE Goal is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion.
roles.Initial_state: A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
roles.Means: The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Path: The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
roles.Place: The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).
roles.Result: A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
roles.Source: The FE Source is the starting point of motion.
roles.Theme: The FE Theme is generally an NP Object. 'Pat threw the china at the wall.'
roles.Time: The time at which the motion of the Theme occurs.

Cause_proliferation_in_number.def: An Agent (or inanimate Cause) affects a Set so that the number of entities that make up the Set changes from an Initial_number to a Final_number.

roles.Agent: The person who causes the Set to increase in number.
roles.Attribute: The scale along which the Set ranges in, i.e., number.
roles.Cause: The force that causes the change.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Manner: Any description of the Agent changing the number of the Set which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and genera
roles.Means: An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the number of the Set.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location where the Agent changes the number of the Set.
roles.Purpose: The purpose for which the proliferating of the number of a Set is performed.
roles.Set: The entity whose amount is being changed.
roles.Time: When the proliferating occurs.

Cause_temperature_change.def: In this frame, an Agent changes the temperature of an Item.

roles.Agent: The Agent performs the intentional act which changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that changes the temperature.
roles.Circumstances: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the temperature change occurs.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The length of time for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.Hot_Cold_source: The Hot_Cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.Item: The Item undergoes the temperature change.
roles.Manner: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
roles.Result: Result is the resultant state of the Agent changing the temperature of the Item.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

Cause_to_amalgamate.def: These words refer to an Agent joining Parts to form a Whole.

roles.Agent: In causative uses of these verbs there is an Agent responsible for amalgamating the Parts.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Manner: This FE identifies the Manner in which the amalgamating occurs.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which the amalgamating occurs.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Part_1: This FE identifies the first of two Parts mentioned.
roles.Part_2: This FE identifies the second of two Parts mentioned.
roles.Parts: This FE identifies the Parts entities being combined, and is often expressed in a single plural NP, usually the direct object of a verb.
roles.Place: The location that the event occurs.
roles.Purpose: The state of affairs that the Agent seeks to bring about by the Amalgamation.
roles.Result: This FE is used for indicating the Result of amalgamating.
roles.Time: The time at which the amalgamation occurs.
roles.Whole: This FE identifies Whole as the entity resulting from combination of Parts.

Cause_to_be_dry.def: An Agent causes a Dryee (either a surface or an entire entity, inside and out) to become dry.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the Dryee to become dry.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of dryness.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Dryee: The Dryee is the entity which has the water removed from it.
roles.Duration: This FE identifies the length of Time that the drying takes.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
roles.Manner: This FE identifies the Manner in which an the Agent dries the Dryee.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which Agent intentionally affects the Dryee and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

Cause_to_be_included.def: An Agent or Cause makes a New_member part of Group.

roles.Agent: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the New_member to become part of the Group.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that is responsible for causing a New_member to enter a Group.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Existing_member: Something that is already a member of the Group and represents the Group as a whole.
roles.Group: The Group is anything that can be conceptualized as a complex collection of parts or ingredients, including through metonymy like containers or locations, which
roles.Manner: The manner in which the Agent acts.
roles.Means: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the inclusion of a New_member.
roles.New_member: An item that becomes a part of the Group.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location in which a New_member is entered into a pre-existing Group.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies what the Agent hopes to accomplish by including a New_member to a Group.
roles.Time: This FE identifies when the inclusion of the New_member to the Group occurs.

Cause_to_be_sharp.def: An Agent or Cause makes a Patient sharper or duller.

roles.Agent: The Agent causes the Patient to become more or less sharp.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of sharpness.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The state of affairs that the Agent is responding to by executing the sharpening act.
roles.Instrument: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient, causing it to change in sharpness.
roles.Manner: The manner in which the Agent changes the sharpness of the Patient.
roles.Means: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the sharpening (or dulling) action.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: The Patient is the entity that is sharpened.
roles.Place: This FE identifies the place where the Agent sharpens the Patient.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent sharpens the Patient.
roles.Result: The resulting configuration of the Patient.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the time when the Agent sharpens Patient.

Cause_to_be_wet.def: An Agent causes a Patient to be wet with a Liquid.

roles.Agent: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the Patient to become wet.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of wetness.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: This FE describes the reason for the state of the Cause_to_be_wet event.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally wets the Patient.
roles.Liquid: The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates or covers the Patient.
roles.Manner: This FE identifies the Manner or way in which the Agent wets the Patient.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which an the Agent wets the Patient
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: The Patient takes up the Liquid through its pores or has the Liquid covering its surface.
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent wets the Patient.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent wets the Patient and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent wets the Patient.

Cause_to_continue.def: An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to continue.

roles.Agent: The individual who causes the Process to continue or the State to be maintained.
roles.Cause: An event that causes the Process or State to be maintained.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The length of time for which the Agent maintain the State or Process.
roles.Instrument: An entity directed by the Agent that maintain the State or Process.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events
roles.Means: The event by which an Agent or Cause maintains the State or Process.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the Process continues.
roles.Process: A Process that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.
roles.Purpose: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by maintaining the State or Process.
roles.State: The State that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.
roles.Time: The time at which the Process continues.

Cause_to_end.def: An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to end.

roles.Agent: The individual who causes the Process or State to end.
roles.Cause: An event that causes the Process or State to end.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The Explanation for why the Process or State is ended.
roles.Manner: The Manner of causing the Process or State to end.
roles.Means: An action of the Agent that causes the Process or State to end.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location where the Process or State is caused to end.
roles.Process: A Process which is ended by the Agent or Cause.
roles.State: A State which is ended by the Agent or Cause.
roles.Time: The Time when the Process or State is ended.

Cause_to_experience.def: An Agent intentionally seeks to bring about an internal mental or emotional state in the Experiencer.

roles.Agent: The Agent is an External Argument of the target word and purposefully arouses an emotional state.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Experiencer: The Experiencer is the person the Agent causes to have a particular emotional state.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent brings about the emotional state.
roles.Manner: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which the Agent affects the Experiencer.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally tries to bring about an internal mental or emotional state.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent affects the Experiencer
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent brings about the emotional state in the Experiencer.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent affects the Experiencer.

Cause_to_fragment.def: An Agent suddenly and often violently separates the Whole_patient into two or more smaller Pieces, resulting in the Whole_patient no longer existing as such.

roles.Agent: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Whole_patient being broken into Pieces.
roles.Cause: An event which leads to the fragmentation of the Whole_patient.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.
roles.Instrument: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Whole_patient to accomplish its fracture.
roles.Manner: Any description of the fracturing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard,
roles.Means: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the breakage.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Pieces: The fragments of the Whole_patient that result from the Agent's action.
roles.Place: This FE identifies the place where the Agent breaks the Whole_patient into pieces.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the break-up of the Whole_patient.
roles.Result: This FE identifies the Result of an event.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the time when the Agent breaks up the Whole_patient.
roles.Whole_patient: The entity which is destroyed by the Agent and that ends up broken into Pieces.

Cause_to_land.def: An Operator maneuvers onto land a Vehicle which typically does not operate on land, e.g., an airplane or boat.

roles.Circumstances: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the landing event itself and any of its part
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Frequency: How often the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.
roles.Goal: Goal is any expression that tells where the Vehicle ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.
roles.Manner: A Manner expression describes a property of landing which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which a Operator lands a Vehicle.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Operator: The Operator maneuvers the vehicle onto land.
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the landing occurs.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.
roles.Source: Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the Operator lands teh Vehicle.
roles.Vehicle: The Vehicle ends up stationary on land. 'She landed the plane on an unoccupied airstrip.'

Cause_to_make_noise.def: An Agent manipulates a Sound_maker or a Cause causes the Sound_maker to emit a sound.

roles.Agent: The individual that manipulates a Sound_maker so that it makes Noise.
roles.Cause: The inanimate force of nature that causes the Sound_maker to produce noise.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
roles.Frequency: The number of times the Sound_maker makes noise per some unit of time.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, soft
roles.Means: An action directly due to the Agent or Cause that results in the Sound_maker emitting noise..
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the sound is produced.
roles.Purpose: The state-of-affairs or action that the Agent wishes to bring about by performing the action.
roles.Sound_maker: The entity that produces the Noise, as a result of the action of the Agent.
roles.Time: The time at which the noise is produced.

Cause_to_make_progress.def: An Agent works on a Project so that it reaches a more advanced and desirable state.

roles.Agent: The individual that brings about the development of the Project.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The period over which the Agent develops the Project.
roles.Explanation: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
roles.Manner: A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way); in addition, it may describe characteristics and states of the Agent tha
roles.Means: The action of the Agent which enables the advancement.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the the Project progresses.
roles.Project: The object or idea that undergoes change due to the efforts of the Agent.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent progresses the Project.
roles.Time: The time at which the progress occurs.

Cause_to_move_in_place.def: An Agent causes a Theme to move with respect to a certain Fixed_location, generally with a certain Periodicity, without undergoing unbounded translational motion or significant alteration of configuration/shape.

roles.Agent: The Agent performs the intentional act.
roles.Bodypart_of_agent: This FE identifies the part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Theme.
roles.Cause: Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the motion in place.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
roles.Explanation: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
roles.Manner: Manner of performing an action
roles.Means: The Means is the way in which the motion in place is instigated.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
roles.Result: This FE identifies the Result of an event.
roles.Theme: Theme identifies the object involved in motion.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

Cause_to_perceive.def: An Agent, Actor, Entity, or Medium causes a Phenomenon to be perceived by a Perceiver.

roles.Actor: An Actor is a sentient being who is exhibiting, possibly uninintentionally, some Phenomenon.
roles.Agent: The Agent intentionally creates a situation in which the Perceiver observes or experiences the Phenomenon.
roles.Co-participant: A Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the Actor or Co-participant Agent.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Entity: An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.
roles.Explanation: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
roles.Frequency: Frequency describes how often the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
roles.Manner: A description of the way in which the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
roles.Means: The instrument or method by which the Perceiver was shown the Phenomenon.
roles.Medium: The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Perceiver: The Perceiver is made to have a perceptual experience by the Agent.
roles.Phenomenon: The Phenomenon is an entity or idea that is perceived by the Perceiver.
roles.Place: The location where the Agent causes the perception of the Perceiver.
roles.Purpose: The purpose of the Agent in creating the perception of the Perceiver.
roles.Time: When the event occurs.

Cause_to_resume.def: An Agent acts so as to cause some process to begin again after an interruption or suspension.

roles.Agent: A sentient being acts with the intention of causing a process to begin again.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that causes the process to resume.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Hiatus: The period of time during which the process is suspended.
roles.Manner: A description of the manner in which the Agent causes the resumption of the Process.
roles.Means: The intentional act performed by the Agent that results in the resumption of the Process.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location where the Agent causes the Process to resume.
roles.Process: The process which begins again after a suspension.
roles.Time: The time at which the process is restarted.

Cause_to_rot.def: An Patient, which is an organic substance, undergoes the natural process of decay due to a Cause (or Agent).

roles.Agent: The Agent intentionally brings about the decay of the Patient.
roles.Cause: An event which causes the Patient to rot.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Instrument: The Agent may use an instrument to bring about the rotting.
roles.Manner: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions compar
roles.Means: An act performed by an Agent, or a sub-event centered around a Cause that leads it to cause the Patient to rot.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: The Patient undergoes decay.
roles.Place: The location at which the Cause acts upon the Patient.
roles.Result: The Result of causing the Patient to rot.
roles.Time: The time at which the Cause causes the Patient to rot.

Cause_to_start.def: A Cause, animate or inanimate, causes a process, the Effect, to begin.

roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect.
roles.Circumstances: The state of the world at the time when the Cause produces the Effect.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Effect: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Cause initiates.
roles.Explanation: The reason why or the way in which the Cause causes the Effect.
roles.Manner: The way in which the Cause causes the Effect.
roles.Means: The Means is the way in which the Cause causes the process to begin.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the Effect occurs.
roles.Purpose: To what end the Cause caused the Effect.
roles.Time: This FE is for the Time when causing to start occurs

Cause_to_wake.def: An Agent or Cause causes a Sleeper to transition from the Sleep_state to wakeful consciousness.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.
roles.Cause: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an intentional act is performed.
roles.Instrument: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: Where the event takes place.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent wakes the Sleeper.
roles.Sleeper: The person or being that is sleeping.
roles.Time: When the event occurs.

Ceasing_to_be.def: An Entity ceases to exist. 'Entire platoons have mysteriously vanished from battle, leaving enemy weapons to slice through empty air.'

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Entity: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.
roles.Explanation: This FE labels the Explanation of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.
roles.Manner: The way in which the Entity disappears.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This is the Place where the new Entity ceases to exist.
roles.Role: The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.
roles.Time: This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity ceases to be.

Certainty.def: This frame concerns a Cognizer's certainty about the correctness of beliefs or expectations.

roles.Cognizer: The Cognizer is the person whose certainty or uncertainty is at issue.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Content: The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.
roles.Explanation: The reason for which the Cognizer is certain.
roles.Expressor: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the mental state of the Cognizer.
roles.Manner: The FE Manner denotes the manner of the certainty or uncertainty.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Topic: The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer has a certain/uncertain belief about.

Change_accessibility.def: An Agent causes a Useful_location to become accessible (or non-accessible) to a Theme to a certain Degree.

roles.Agent: The Agent blocks access to the Useful_location.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Instrument: The Agent uses the Instrument to block access, often by placing the Instrument such that it cannot be traversed.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, soft
roles.Means: An action carried out by the Agent to bring about the change in accessibility.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The general Place where the blocking or allowing of access occurs.
roles.Portal: The Agent may regulate access to the Useful_location by regulating access to a Portal, including a part of the portal that could block potential Themes, such as
roles.Purpose: The Purpose for which the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.
roles.Time: The Time when the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.
roles.Useful_location: The Useful_location is the place the Theme is headed towards and the Agent has changed the accessibility of.

Change_direction.def: A Theme that is in motion assumes a new Direction in which it moves.

roles.Circumstances: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the change of direction event itself and any of its participants, a
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Direction: The new direction in which the Theme continues its motion.
roles.Explanation: A factor which explains the change of direction of the Theme.
roles.Frequency: The number of times that a change of direction occurs.
roles.Goal: Any expression which indicates where the Theme ends up as a result of the change of direction.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and gene
roles.Means: An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The Place is the setting where the change of direction during the Theme's motion occurs.
roles.Purpose: The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.
roles.Result: The situation that results from the change of direction
roles.Source: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
roles.Theme: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not required to be
roles.Time: The time at which the change of direction takes place.

Change_event_duration.def: In this frame, an Agent or Cause changes the duration of an Event.

roles.Agent: The sentient entity that changes the duration of the Event.
roles.Cause: An event that causes the change in Event duration.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Event: The Event's duration is changed. 'Don't let him prolong the discussion to an absurd length.'
roles.Explanation: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change of duration.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event causing the change of the Event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably,
roles.Means: An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Event's duration.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Purpose: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by changing the duration of the Event.
roles.Time: The time at which the change in duration of the Event is caused.

Change_event_time.def: In this frame, an Agent or Cause changes the timing of an Event.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the animate entity which brings about the change in time of the Event.
roles.Cause: The Cause is the non-sentient force which brings about the change of time for the Event.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Destination_time: The Destination_time is the time at which the Event actually occurs.
roles.Event: The Event is the occurrence which changes time.
roles.Explanation: The Explanation is the reason or explanation for why the Event occurs at a different time.
roles.Manner: The Manner is the way in which the time change takes place.
roles.Means: The Means describe the way in which the time change is accomplished.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the expected time of the Event changes.
roles.Purpose: The state-of-affairs that the Agent intends to bring about by changing the time the Event will take place.
roles.Time: The time at which the delay occurred.

Change_of_consistency.def: In this frame a Patient changes its consistency.

roles.Circumstances: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The Explanation for which the Patient changes consistency.
roles.Manner: The Manner in which the Patient changes consistency.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: Patient is the entity that undergoes a change.
roles.Place: Where the the Patient changes consistency.
roles.Result: This FE indicates the Result of the change of consistency of the Patient 'The liquid gelled into a semi-solid mass.'
roles.Time: When the Patient changes consistency.

Change_of_leadership.def: This frame concerns the appointment of a New_leader or removal from office of an Old_leader.

roles.Body: A group of individuals who are elected or appointed to perform some function of governance.
roles.Circumstances: This frame element describes the situation that brought about the change of leadership.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Function: The Function is the purpose the New_leader will fufill.
roles.Manner: This FE is used for the Manner of performing an action.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which the Selector accomplishes the change of leadership.
roles.New_leader: With words denoting appointment to a position, the New_leader is typically the object of verbs.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Old_leader: With words denoting removal (or attempted removal) from office of a leader, the Old_leader is typically the direct object of verbs, or occurs in a PP Complement
roles.Old_order: The FE Old_order identifies the political order that existed before the change of leadership occurs.
roles.Place: Where the change takes place. 'The crew mutinied out in the middle of the Atlantic, the scoundrels.'
roles.Result: This FE is used for indicating the Result of an event.
roles.Role: Frequently the Old_leader or New_leader is referred to only by his/her role.
roles.Selector: The Selector (most commonly a group of people) is responsible for a change in leadership.
roles.Time: When the change takes place. 'The 2000 coup against the dictator was led by former president Smith.'

Change_of_phase.def: In this frame a Patient undergoes a change of phase.

roles.Circumstances: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the phase change occurs.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Manner: The Manner in which the Patient changes phase.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: Patient is the entity that undergoes a change of phase.
roles.Place: Where the Patient changes phase.
roles.Result: The FE Result indicates the result of the change of phase.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time at which the Patient changes phase.

Change_of_quantity_of_possession.def: This frame describes a general situation in which an Owner either increases or decreases their amount of a Possession.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: This FE denotes a proposition from which the event of increasing or decreasing in quantity logically follows.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Owner: The Owner is the entity that contains within itself or controls the Possession.
roles.Place: The Place where the Possession undergoes a change in quantity.
roles.Possession: The Possession is the physical or metaphoric object that increases or decreases in quantity.
roles.Time: The Time when the Possession undergoes a change in quantity.

Change_of_temperature.def: In this frame, the temperature of an Item changes.

roles.Cause: An event or state-of-affairs that leads to the change in temperature of the Item.
roles.Circumstances: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the temperature change occurs
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The span of time in which the Item is changing temperature.
roles.Item: The entity whose temperature changes.
roles.Manner: The manner in which the Item changes temperature.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the Item changes temperature.
roles.Result: The state of the Item that results from the temperature change.
roles.Temperature: The scalar property that the Item possesses.
roles.Time: The time at which the change in temperature occurs.

Change_operational_state.def: A Device or machine is put in (or out of) service either by a volitional Agent or by a Cause event or force acting on the Device.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the person who changes the operational state of the Device.
roles.Cause: Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the Device to begin to operate.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Device: The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.
roles.Explanation: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the event of the Device's being caused to operate or cease to operate logically follows.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and gene
roles.Means: An action done by the Agent in order to cause the Device to being to operate.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The Place in which the Device is put into or out of operation.
roles.Purpose: The FE Purpose denotes a state of affairs that the Agent wants to bring about by putting the Device into operation.
roles.Time: The Time when a Device is put into or out of operation.

Change_position_on_a_scale.def: This frame consists of words that indicate the change of an Item's position on a scale (the Attribute) from a starting point (Initial_value) to an end point (Final_value).

roles.Attribute: The Attribute is a scalar property that the Item possesses.'Oil rose in price by 2%.'
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Difference: The distance by which an Item changes its position on the scale.'Oil rose in price by 2%.'
roles.Duration: The length of time over which the change takes place.
roles.Explanation: The situation or state-of-affairs that results in the change in quantity described in this instance of the frame.
roles.Final_state: A description that presents the Item's state after the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.
roles.Final_value: The position on the scale where the Item ends up.
roles.Initial_state: A description that presents the Item's state before the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.
roles.Initial_value: The initial position on the scale from which the Item moves away.
roles.Item: The entity that has a position on the scale.
roles.Manner: Manner of performing an action
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: A location where Attribute is measured
roles.Result: Result. of an event
roles.Time: The Time is the time-frame in which the change of position occurs.
roles.Value_range: A portion of the scale, typically identified by its end points, along which the values of the Attribute fluctuate.

Change_post-state.def: The frame represents the result state of the Entity after event represented by the Undergo_change frame.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Change_posture.def: A Protagonist changes the overall position and posture of the body.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Goal: This FE is used for any expressions that indicate the endpoint of the posture change.
roles.Manner: Any description of the change in posture which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comp
roles.Means: An action of the Protagonist whereby they achieve the change of posture.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Protagonist: The individual whose posture changes.
roles.Purpose: The Purpose for which a Protagonist assumes a posture.
roles.Result: The final state of the Protagonist after the change of posture.
roles.Source: Source is used for expressions that indicate the starting point of the change of posture.
roles.Time: The Time at which the Protagonist changes posture.

Change_resistance.def: An Agent changes a Patient's ability to resist literal or figurative attack.

roles.Agent: The Agent makes the Patient more resistant to attack.
roles.Cause: An event which causes the Patient to become more resistant.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Manner: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions compar
roles.Means: An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Patient.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: The Patient is the entity that is being made more resistant.
roles.Place: The location at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.
roles.Result: The resultant state of the action.
roles.Time: The time at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.

Change_tool.def: An Agent changes Tools, from the Old_tool to a New_tool.

roles.Agent: The individual that changes their situation.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Manner: Any description of the Agent's change which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions compari
roles.Means: The action of the Agent which brings about a change.
roles.New_tool: The tool that the Agent ends up using.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Old_tool: The tool that the Agent had been using.
roles.Place: This FE identifies the place where the Agent makes a change.
roles.Purpose: The aim of the Agent when they carry out the change.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.
roles.Tools: The entities controlled by an Agent to achieve some Purpose.

Chaos.def: The lexical units in this frame have to do with an Entity being in a State of order or disorder.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The amount of time in which the Entity exists in the State
roles.Entity: The object or phenomenon which exists in the State of disorder.

Choosing.def: A Cognizer decides upon the Chosen (either an item or a course of action) out of a set of Possibilities .

Circumscribed_existence.def: An Entity is understood to be experienceable within a particular set of delimited Circumstances, which may be more narrowly expressed by a Time, Place.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").

roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: A spacial characterization of the Circumstances of the existence of the Entity.
roles.Time: A temporal characterization of the circumstances of the existence of an Entity.

roles.Charges: Charges identifies the infraction or offense for which the Defendant is summoned.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").

roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: Place is the location where the Defendant is issued the citation or summons.
roles.Time: The Time at which the Defendant is issued the citation or summons.

roles.Claimant: The Claimant asserts rights or priviliges, typically ownership, over some Property.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Offender: The individual who is accused or convicted of a Crime.
roles.Place: The location at which the Executive_authority grants clemency.
roles.Purpose: An action that the Executive_authority intends to accomplish by granting clemency.
roles.Time: The time at which clemency is granted. 'In addition to Ms. White, 55, Mr. Pataki granted clemency yesterday to three men serving long prison terms for offenses

Clothing.def: This frame refers to clothing and its characteristics, including anything that people conventionally wear.

Cogitation.def: A person, the Cognizer, thinks about a Topic over a period of time.

roles.Medium: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed.
roles.Message: An expression of the commitment made by the Speaker expresses the frame element Message.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location in which the Speaker makes the commitment.
roles.Purpose: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by taking on the commitment.
roles.Speaker: The Speaker is the person who commits him/herself to do something.
roles.Time: The time period during which the Speaker makes the commitment.
roles.Topic: Topic expressions are not very frequent in this frame.

Committing_crime.def: A Perpetrator (generally intentionally) commits a Crime, i.e.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Crime: An act, generally intentional, that has been formally forbidden by law.
roles.Explanation: A state of affairs that the Perpetrator is responding to in their Crime.
roles.Frequency: The frequency with which a Crime is committed.
roles.Instrument: The Instrument used in committing the crime.
roles.Manner: A description of secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
roles.Means: An action performed by the Perpetrator in order to accomplish the Crime.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Perpetrator: The individual that commits a Crime. 'How can he commit treason against the King of England in a foreign country , if he is not English?' 'He perpetrated a crim
roles.Place: The location where the Crime occurs. 'We have jurisdiction over crimes committed in Woodside County.'
roles.Purpose: The action that the Perpetrator was trying to accomplish in the Crime.
roles.Time: When the Crime was committed. 'A murder perpetrated at 1:08AM this morning was not investigated until noon today.'

Commonality.def: This frame contains words that describe a set of individuals which possess some Commonality, generally a common attribute.

roles.Commonality: This FE denotes an object or attribute which is jointly posessed by the Entities.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Entities: This FE denotes the people in possession of the Commonality.
roles.Entity_1: One of the possesors of the Commonality. Can be singular or plural. 'He shares a home with us.'
roles.Entity_2: One of the possesors of the Commonality. Can be singular or plural. 'He shares a home with us.'
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Communicate_categorization.def: A Speaker communicates a message stating an Item's membership in a Category, i.e., asserts that the Item has the defining characteristics of the Category.

roles.Category: The class of entities with characteristics that match those of the Item according to the portrayal of the Speaker.
roles.Circumstances: The Circumstances under which the categorization is made.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.
roles.Item: The entity that the Speaker portrays as belonging to a Category.
roles.Manner: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects
roles.Means: An action taken by the Speaker through which they communicate that the Item fits into a particular Category.
roles.Medium: The piece of text in which a Speaker communicates their categorization of the Item.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the Speaker characterizes the Item
roles.Speaker: The individual that communicates the message concerning the Category of an Item.
roles.Time: The point in time at which the Speaker makes a characterization of the Item.

Communication.def: A Communicator conveys a Message to an Addressee; the Topic and Medium of the communication also may be expressed.

roles.Addressee: The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.
roles.Communicator: The sentient entity that uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to the Addressee.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: Duration is the length of time during which the communication takes place.
roles.Frequency: This FE describes the number of times per unit of time that the Communicator conveys a Message.
roles.Manner: The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.
roles.Means: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.
roles.Medium: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
roles.Message: Message is a proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location where the act of communication occurs.
roles.Purpose: The Purpose for which a Communicator communicates.
roles.Time: The time at which the communication takes place.
roles.Topic: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains.

Communication_manner.def: The words in this frame describe Manners of verbal communication.

roles.Addressee: Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker is communicating.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The amount of time that the communicative event lasts.
roles.Manner: Manner of performing an action
roles.Means: The action that the Speaker performs in order to communicate in the particular way described by the target.
roles.Message: Message is the content which is communicated by the Speaker.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the communication event takes place.
roles.Result: This FE identifies the Result of an event.
roles.Speaker: Speaker is the sentient entity that produces a Message or communicates about a Topic.
roles.Time: The time at which the communication event takes place.
roles.Topic: Topic is the subject matter of the communicated Message.

Communication_means.def: This frame concerns Communicators communicating with each other with the aid of a Means of communication such as a telephone.

roles.Addressee: Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated.
roles.Communicator: This FE is the person who uses the Means of communication to deliver the Message to the Addressee.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: This FE identifies the Explanation for using the means of communication.
roles.Manner: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which an action is carried out.
roles.Means: This Frame Element refers to the Instrument of Communication that is used by the Communicator (and Addressee).
roles.Message: This FE identifies the content that the Communicator communicates to the Addressee.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Topic: Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains.

Communication_noise.def: This frame contains words for types of noise which can be used to characterize verbal communication.

roles.Addressee: The Addressee refers to the one toward whom the Communication_noise is directed.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
roles.Manner: Manner describes the manner or style in which the Communication_noise is delivered.
roles.Means: The Means by which the Speaker communicates.
roles.Message: Message has a number of different realizations in this frame, including that-clauses, direct quotes, infinitival complements, for-to phrases, and NP Objects.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where an event occurs.
roles.Speaker: Speaker is the sentient entity that delivers the Message.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time where the Communication noise event occurs.
roles.Topic: Topic occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by about.
roles.Voice: The Voice describes the Speaker's utterance or other message-encoded production.

Communication_response.def: This frame deals with a Speaker communicating a reply or response, a Message, to some prior communication or action, the Trigger.

roles.Addressee: This is the person to whom the response is communicated.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: The Duration of the communication response.
roles.Manner: Manner of performing an action
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by the Speaker achieves the communication of the response Message .
roles.Message: The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location in which the Speaker makes a verbal response.
roles.Purpose: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.
roles.Speaker: The Speaker is the sentient entity that communicates the reply or response.
roles.Time: The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.
roles.Topic: Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun Target:'My boss still hasn't given me an answer about a promotion.'
roles.Trigger: The Trigger is the prior communication or action to which a response is given.

Commutation.def: An Executive_authority exchanges one penalty, the Original_punishment, for another less severe one, the New_punishment.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Executive_authority: The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to commute punishments.
roles.Explanation: A state of affairs that the Executive_authority is responding to in commuting the Original_punishment.
roles.Manner: Any description of the commutation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing e
roles.Means: An action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the commutation.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Original_punishment: The punishment the Offender was originally sentenced to.
roles.Place: The location where the Executive_authority commutes the Original_punishment.
roles.Time: The time at which the Original_punishment is commuted.

Commutative_process.def: LUs in this frame describe a commutative operation of arithmetic, e.g.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Term1: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.
roles.Term2: The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.
roles.Terms: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation.

Commutative_statement.def: LUs in this frame describe a stative relationship between two numbers,Term1 and Term2 or, collectively, Terms, via a commutative arithmetic operation.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Result: The number or role of a number that comes from the interaction of Term1 and Term2 via a commutative operation.
roles.Term1: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.
roles.Term2: The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.
roles.Terms: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation.

Compatibility.def: Item-1 and Item-2 are compatible with each other if they can exist or function together in some context without problems, conflict, or other undesirable situation.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Item_1: The Frame Element Item_1 marks the grammatically more prominent of the two entities, i.e.the subject in active clauses, when they are expressed separately.
roles.Item_2: The Frame Element Item_2 marks the grammatically less prominent of the Items when they are expressed separately.
roles.Items: This FE is used when the Items are expressed jointly in a phrase, either a plural or a coordinated NP.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Parameter: This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate a Parameter or respect in which the Items are said to be compatible, not in conflict.

Competition.def: This frame is concerned with the idea that people (Participant_1, Participant_2, or Participants) participate in an organized, rule-governed activity (the Competition) in order to achieve some advantageous outcome (often the Prize).

roles.Competition: This FE is used for the name of the competition.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Duration: This FE is used to describe the length of time over which competition occurs.
roles.Frequency: This FE expresses how often the Competition occurs.
roles.Manner: The way the Participants compete.
roles.Means: The action the Participants (or Participant_1) are involved in that constitutes a Competition.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Participant_1: This FE identifies the first (or only) participant in a competition.
roles.Participant_2: This FE identifies the second participant in a competition.
roles.Participants: This FE is used for plural NP participants in a competition.
roles.Place: Where the event takes place. A constituent tagged as Place may require annotation on a secondary FE-layer. 'First layer: John's first competition at Wimbledon a
roles.Purpose: This FE is used to describe the intended outcome of the competition.
roles.Time: The period of time when the Competition occurs.

Complaining.def: A Complainer communicates their negative emotional reaction to some state of affairs in a Complaint to an Addressee.

roles.Addressee: The Addressee is the person to whom the Complaint is communicated.
roles.Complainer: The Complainer is the sentient entity that produces the Complaint (whether spoken or written).
roles.Complaint: The lamentable situation that the Complainer is communicating to the Addressee.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes.
roles.Frequency: Frequency is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
roles.Manner: Any description of the complaining event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descri
roles.Means: An act whereby the Complainer makes a complaint.
roles.Medium: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Complainer to transmit the Complaint.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE specifies the location where the complaining takes place.
roles.Result: An event or state which results from the complaining.
roles.Time: The Time when the complaint is made. 'Now yesterday I pissed and moaned about Rolling Stone magazines choice for the number 1 song of all time. '
roles.Topic: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Complaint pertains.

Completeness.def: A Whole, an entity with a substructure, is assessed for whether or not it has all the necessary parts that are defined for it or for an entity of its kind.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Time: The interval of time when the completeness of the entity is assessed.
roles.Whole: The entity that is being assessed for having all its necessary parts or not.

Compliance.def: This frame concerns Acts and State_of_Affairs for which Protagonists are responsible and which either follow or violate some set of rules or Norms.

roles.Act: This FE identifies the Act that is judged to be in or out of compliance with the Norms.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: The Explanation for complying with the Norm.
roles.Manner: This FE identifies the Manner in which the compliance occurs.
roles.Means: This FE identifies the Means by which the compliance is (or is not) accomplished.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Norm: This FE identifies the rules or Norms that ought to guide a person's behavior.
roles.Protagonist: The Protagonist's behavior is in or out of compliance with norms.
roles.Result: This FE identifies the Result of compliance.
roles.State_of_affairs: A State_of_affairs may violate a law or rule.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the Time when the act of compliance or non-compliance occurs.

Concessive.def: A speaker marks a Conceded_state_of_affairs as being or implying a contradiction to the Main_assertion.

roles.Conceded_state_of_affairs: A proposition or set of propositions that the speaker wants the addressee to believe or take for granted.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Main_assertion: The statement that the speaker wishes to assert or offer as their main contribution to the discourse, which is be modified or hedged in some way by the Conceded
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Topic: An entity which metonymically stands in for an associated Statement.

Condition_symptom_relation.def: A Patient has a Medical_condition that can be understood by its Symptoms.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: Explanation for why a Symptom(s) or Medical_condition(s) occur.
roles.Frequency: The commonality of a Medical_condition or Symptom
roles.Medical_condition: A holistic description of the medical state of the Patient (or a part of the state of the Patient), which may or may not indicate the cause of a deviation from
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Patient: The person who has a Medical_condition associated with Symptom.
roles.Place: The location where a Medical_condition presents.
roles.Symptom: A deviation from normal function or feeling which is noticed by a Patient or physician, indicating the presence of a Medical_condition
roles.Time: When a Symptom or Medical_condition occurs.

Conditional_occurrence.def: A Consequence is presented as occurring if the Profiled_possibility occurs.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Consequence: The situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Profiled_possibility: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Negated_possibility.

Conduct.def: An Agent acts in a certain Manner either generally or under some particular Circumstances.

roles.Agent: This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.
roles.Circumstances: This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.
roles.Manner: This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves.
roles.Means: The way in which the Agent behaves in the specified manner.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.
roles.Time: The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.

Conferring_benefit.def: A Benefactor confers a Beneficial_situation to a Beneficiary.

roles.Benefactor: The Benefactor is the person or thing that gives an advantage to the Beneficiary.
roles.Beneficial_situation: The Beneficial_situation is the item or action that is given to or done for the Beneficiary by the Benefactor.
roles.Beneficiary: The Beneficiary is person or thing that receives an advantage from the Benefactor.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Confronting_problem.def: An Agent becomes involved in an Issue which has negative consequences for them.

roles.Agent: The Agent is the person who is acting to deal with the Issue.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Explanation: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
roles.Frequency: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.
roles.Issue: This FE identifies the Issue that the Agent deals with.
roles.Manner: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions compar
roles.Means: This FE identifies the way in which an Agent goes about facing the Issue.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the Place where the intentional act occurs.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the reason why the Agent confronts the issue.
roles.Result: The Result describes the resulting outcome of the confronting act.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

Connecting_architecture.def: An entity is integrated into a building as a Part of a (possibly unexpressed) Whole which may refer to the whole building or merely to a sub-part of the building.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Goal: The Goal is one of the Connected_locations treated as a goal 'Finally they corner us as we reach the escalator to the first floor.'
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Part: A Part of a larger architectural unit, the Whole.
roles.Source: The Source is one of the Connected_locations treated as source.

Connectors.def: The Connector is an artifact created to affix a Connected_item or to bind onto a Fixed_location and is primarily so used.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Connector: Connector identifies the entity or substance that forms the bond that maintains the Item in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a "with"-PP.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Conquering.def: This frame describes a Theme losing its autonomy and perhaps sustaining material damage as the result of a successful invasion on the behalf of a Conqueror.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Conqueror: The Conqueror is the entity that overtakes the Theme.
roles.Frequency: Frequency is the number of times the Conquering event occurs per some unit of time.
roles.Instrument: The tool used by the Conqueror to seize the Theme.
roles.Manner: The manner in which the Conqueror takes over the Theme.
roles.Means: The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Conqueror.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: The location where the Conqueror takes over the Theme.
roles.Purpose: The reason why the Conqueror seized the Theme.
roles.Theme: The Theme is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Conqueror.
roles.Time: The Time at which the Conqueror seizes the Theme.

Contact_information.def: A way to reach a person or business: phone number, email, handle, address.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Contact: The number, email, handle or address.
roles.Medium: Phone, email, app.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Contacting.def: A Communicator (whose Location may be indicated) directs a Communication to an Addressee at a particular Address.

roles.Address: This FE is used for a (metaphorical) place in a system of communication where Communicators and Addressees can access the system.
roles.Addressee: The person that receives the message from the Communicator.'The company must be able to call potential customers.'
roles.Communication: The information that the Communicator wishes to impart to the Addressee, often to get a particular response.
roles.Communicator: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a message to another person.'He wrote to John.'
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Frequency: The number of times a Communicator contacts the Addressee per unit of time.
roles.Manner: Any description of the nature of the action (e.g.
roles.Means: An action of the Communicator that enables them to make contact.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Place: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.
roles.Purpose: This FE identifies the Purpose for the Communicator contacting the Addressee.
roles.Time: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.
roles.Topic: This is the subject matter to which the message pertains.

Containers.def: This frame covers entities which are prototypically conceived of and created to fulfill the function of containing--i.e.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Container: Container is an object which is conventionally used as a container.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").

Containing.def: In this frame a Container holds within its physical boundaries the Contents.

roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Container: The Container is the physical object which holds within its boundaries the Contents 'The box holds three hundred pictures.'
roles.Contents: The Contents is the substance or objects contained within the physical bounds of the Container.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Time: The time at which the Container holds the Contents.

Contingency.def: The answer to one open question, the Outcome, is dictated (partially or completely) by the answer to another open question, the Determinant, i.e.

roles.Circumstances: The conditions under which the Determinant dictates the Outcome.
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.Determinant: An open question that determines the Outcome.
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Outcome: An open question that is (to some degree) predictable from the Determinant.

Continued_state_of_affairs.def: A State_of_affairs has held and continues to hold up to the Reference_occasion.

roles.Circumstances: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants
roles.Condition: A condition that must hold for the frame to happen ("when the ladder comes back").
roles.New_value: The new value when the frame states a change of an earlier fact ("moved to the 14th").
roles.Reference_occasion: The time or event (normally speech time) with respect to which the State_of_affairs is located.
roles.State_of_affairs: A state which holds prior to and up through the Reference_occasion.

Contrary_circumstances.def: An Event takes place despite the existence of an Adversity that would otherwise support Contrary_circumstances or results.
